prompt.v: A patient is given 100 mg of a medicine with a half-life of 12 hours. After how many hours are 45 mg left? Give the time to 1 decimal place.

problems.explain: Every 12 hours halves it, so after t hours it is 100 × (1/2) to the power t/12. Set that equal to 45 and divide by 100: (1/2) to the power t/12 is 9/20. Take ln of both sides; the power comes down: (t/12) ln(1/2) = ln(9/20), so t = 12 ln(9/20) / ln(1/2) ≈ 13.824. So it takes about 13.8 hours.

problems.explain: Set 5000e to the power 0.08t equal to 20000 and divide by 5000: e to the power 0.08t is 4. ln undoes e, so take ln of both sides: 0.08t = ln 4, and t = ln 4 / 0.08 ≈ 17.3287. So it takes about 17.33 years.

prompt.v: A patient is given 60 mg of a medicine with a half-life of 10 hours. After how many hours are 25 mg left? Give the time to 2 decimal places.

problems.explain: Every 10 hours halves it, so after t hours it is 60 × (1/2) to the power t/10. Set that equal to 25 and divide by 60: (1/2) to the power t/10 is 5/12. Take ln of both sides; the power comes down: (t/10) ln(1/2) = ln(5/12), so t = 10 ln(5/12) / ln(1/2) ≈ 12.6303. So it takes about 12.63 hours.
